target: WIN-002 citation re-point (monitor.py -> snapshotted live-power dashboard) + WIN-047/WIN-055 redshift-scale-family scoping half-clause (curmudgeon-deferred deeper tag reconsideration explicitly NOT applied)

patches.description: ISS-3047 (curmudgeon c5 minor hole, WIN-002): detail_evidence cited monitor.py Domain #1 hardcoded predicted=observed=7.83, but monitor.py/pull_data.py are no longer captured in raw-text/ (verified: raw-text/ currently holds only page snapshots 01-home.txt through 08-live-power.txt plus WIN-066-v51.txt -- no monitor.py or pull_data.py). Re-pointed the citation to the snapshotted live-power dashboard instead, which independently corroborates the identical finding: raw-text/08-live-power.txt line 201-202 shows 'Domain: Schumann Frequency / Predicted: 7.83 Hz | Observed: 7.83 Hz', and the same file's own audit section (line 288) explicitly flags this as a 'PRED=OBS IDENTITY CHECK' -- the dome's own audit language corroborating our finding. This is suggested_fix option 2 from the ISS ('re-point citation to the snapshotted live-power dashboard'); option 1 (re-capture monitor.py/pull_data.py into raw-text/) was not pursued since the live-power dashboard already contains an equally strong (arguably stronger, since it's the dome's own self-audit) citation for the same claim.

patches.find_pattern: H₀ ≈ 70 km/s/Mpc is measured from standard cosmology. The dome model adopts this value without derivation. It has no photon-aether interaction equation, no redshift mechanism, and no galaxy-scale physics.\n\nIndependent of the scientific critique above, this claim also fails our post-hoc test on structural grounds. The numerical value is textbook physics (Part 3.1b, \"trivial-transcription test\"): it appears in undergraduate references and widely indexed resources, so there is no meaningful sense in which the dome monitor script \"predicted\" it before reading the data. Under the dome author's own definition (\"prediction was timestamped before confirming data was pulled\"), the dome DOES automate a redshift check — its live-power \"Aetheric Redshift Scale\" domain reports Predicted 4283 Mpc vs. Observed 4319 Mpc, Status PASS, sourced to the Virgo cluster (NED) — but 4283 Mpc is exactly c/H₀(70), the textbook Hubble radius.

patches.description: ISS-3049 (curmudgeon c7 minor residual, WIN-055, companion to ISS-3048/WIN-047): identical shared paragraph (verified byte-identical to the WIN-047 instance via grep -c, count=2 in data/wins.json before this patch) gets the same scoping half-clause, naming WIN-055 specifically and noting its own code_analysis.monitoring tag is also 'none'. tldr_evidence: Three small curmudgeon-flagged residuals on already-landed patches: WIN-002 cited a source file (monitor.py) that isn't captured in our raw-text mirror, and WIN-047/WIN-055 both contained an unscoped sentence that could misleadingly imply those specific WINs have automated dome-side monitoring when they don't.
tldr_verdict: All three are citation/wording corrections, not verdict changes. WIN-002 now cites the snapshotted live-power dashboard (which independently confirms the same predicted=observed hardcoding). WIN-047 and WIN-055 now scope the automation sentence to the redshift-scale domain family rather than implying it applies to the WIN itself.
investigation_notes: ISS-3047: confirmed via `find . -type d -iname raw-text` + `ls raw-text/` that the only captured files are page snapshots (01-home.txt ... 08-live-power.txt, WIN-066-v51.txt); grep -i '7.83|schumann|predicted' raw-text/08-live-power.txt located the corroborating Domain 1 panel (line 201-202) and the dome's own 'PRED=OBS IDENTITY CHECKS' audit callout (line 288).

ISS-3048/ISS-3049: confirmed via grep -c on data/wins.json that the flagged paragraph ('the dome DOES automate a redshift check ... textbook Hubble radius.') occurs exactly twice in the file (WIN-047 and WIN-055, byte-identical), matching curmudgeon's description of a shared/companion residual. Confirmed both WINs' code_analysis.monitoring field is 'none' before writing the scoping clause, so the parenthetical is accurate.

All three patches simulated against a scratch copy of data/wins.json (python replace + json.load) before this EXP was written, to confirm find_pattern uniqueness (count=1 each) and that the resulting file remains valid JSON after substitution.
test_coverage: tests/run.sh will be run post-write per the self-test step; these are wins.json prose/citation edits (no layer counts, rates, ransomware numbers, http_data, or classifier changes) so no new test is required, but existing WIN-002/047/055 content-consistency checks (if any) should still pass unchanged since verdicts and code_analysis fields are untouched.
